# 1. Importing data --------------------------------------------

```{r}
install.packages(c("readr", "dplyr", "tidyr", "ggplot2", "stringr", "forcats", "lubridate", "tibble", "scales"))
```

```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)
library(lubridate)
library(tibble)
library(scales)
```

```{r}
frontiers_raw <- read_csv("EXDragonFrontiersProductsAndPrices.csv")

prismatic_raw <- read_csv("SVPrismaticEvolutionsProductsAndPrices.csv")
```


```{r}
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
set_colours <- c("EX Dragon Frontiers" = "#284fa8", "Prismatic Evolutions" = "#c048db")
```

## 1.2 Helpers ----

```{r}
# Helper: print a heading in the console
section <- function(title) {
  cat("\n", strrep("=", 70), "\n", title, "\n", strrep("=", 70), "\n", sep = "")
}

# Helper: show a plot and save it as a PNG
show_plot <- function(p, file, width = 9, height = 5) {
  print(p)
  ggsave(file.path("eda_plots", file), p, width = width, height = height, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
}

# Helper: print a whole table (all rows) in the console
show_table <- function(df, title = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(title)) cat("\n--", title, "--\n")
  print(as.data.frame(df), row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)
  invisible(df)
}
```

```{r}
compare_counts <- function(col) {
  bind_rows(`EX Dragon Frontiers`            = count(frontiers_raw,  value = .data[[col]]),
            `Prismatic Evolutions` = count(prismatic_raw, value = .data[[col]]),
            .id = "set") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = set, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
}

show_table(compare_counts("extRarity"), "Rarity labels")
show_table(compare_counts("extCardType"), "Card type labels")
show_table(compare_counts("extStage"), "Stage labels")
show_table(compare_counts("subTypeName"), "Printing labels")
show_table(compare_counts("extResistance"), "Resistance labels")

```

# *More specificity in product and print type for modern era - pokeball print finish in Prismatic for example

```{r}
  summarise(across(c(extNumber, extRarity, extHP, extWeakness, extResistance,
```

```{r}
show_table(bind_rows(frontiers_raw, prismatic_raw) %>%
             filter(is.na(marketPrice)) %>%

```
# The booster and Charizard chase card don't have recent sales because they are so rare -- removing them would defeat the purpose, since they're the most valuable items -- so we need to keep whatever value is available for it (even if it's lowPrice or midPrice)


# 3 Cleaning and wrangling ------------------------------------

## 3.1 Cleaning ----

```{r}
#Remove html junk --> thank you internet <3

strip_html <- function(x) {
  x %>% str_replace_all("<br>", " ") %>% str_replace_all("<[^>]+>", "") %>% str_squish()
}


trainer_stages <- c("Supporter", "Tool", "Stadium", "Trainer")

clean_set <- function(df, set_name) {
  df %>%
    mutate(across(any_of("extUPC"), as.character)) %>%
    select(-categoryId, -groupId, -imageCount, -imageUrl, -url, -cleanName) %>%
    mutate(
      set        = set_name,
      modifiedOn = as_datetime(modifiedOn),
       # --- Trainer / Energy labels -------------------------------------------
      # Dragon Frontiers: the sub-type is reliable in extStage, so use it
      # (generic "Trainer" items like Switch / Old Rod become "Item").
      extCardType = case_when(
        extStage %in% trainer_stages   ~ recode(extStage, Trainer = "Item"),
        extStage == "Special Energy"   ~ "Special Energy",
        TRUE                           ~ extCardType
      ),
      # Prismatic: "Trainer - Item" -> "Item", "Pokemon Tool" -> "Tool"
      extCardType = extCardType %>%
        str_remove("^Trainer - ") %>%
        str_replace("Pokemon Tool", "Tool"),
      # stage only applies to Pokemon
      extStage = if_else(extStage %in% c("Basic", "Stage 1", "Stage 2"), extStage, NA_character_),

      product_class = case_when(
        extRarity == "Code Card"                                   ~ "Code card",
        is.na(extNumber)                                           ~ "Sealed product",
        extCardType %in% c("Item", "Stadium", "Supporter", "Tool") ~ "Trainer",
        extCardType %in% c("Special Energy", "Energy")             ~ "Energy",
        TRUE                                                       ~ "Pokemon"
      ),
      # --- Fix impossible / placeholder values -------------------------------
      extHP         = if_else(product_class == "Pokemon", extHP, NA_real_),  # 0 HP -> NA
      extResistance = na_if(extResistance, "None"),

      # --- Card number & names ----------------------------------------------
      card_no    = as.integer(str_extract(extNumber, "^\\d+")),
      set_size   = as.integer(str_extract(extNumber, "\\d+$")),
      is_secret  = card_no > set_size,
      is_delta   = str_detect(name, "\\(Delta Species\\)"),
      card_name  = name %>%
        str_remove(" \\(Delta Species\\)") %>%
        str_remove(" \\((Poke|Master) Ball Pattern\\)") %>%
        str_remove(" - \\d+/\\d+$"),
      is_ex        = str_detect(card_name, " ex$"),
      is_gold_star = str_detect(card_name, " Star$"),

      # finish = printing + Prismatic's ball patterns
      finish = case_when(
        str_detect(name, "Master Ball Pattern") ~ "Master Ball Pattern",
        str_detect(name, "Poke Ball Pattern")   ~ "Poke Ball Pattern",
        TRUE                                    ~ subTypeName
      ),
      across(any_of(c("extAttack1", "extAttack2", "extAttack3", "extCardText")), strip_html),
      weak_code   = str_sub(extWeakness, 1, 1),     # "Rx2" -> "R"
      resist_code = str_sub(extResistance, 1, 1),   # "F-30" -> "F"

      # --- Analysis price -----------------------------------------------------
      price        = coalesce(marketPrice, lowPrice),
      price_source = case_when(!is.na(marketPrice) ~ "market (recent sales)",
                               !is.na(lowPrice)    ~ "lowest listing (no sales)",
                               TRUE                ~ "none"),
      thin_market_flag = lowPrice > 2 * marketPrice
    )
}

frontiers <- clean_set(frontiers_raw, "EX Dragon Frontiers")
prismatic <- clean_set(prismatic_raw, "Prismatic Evolutions")

# Check the cleaning worked
show_table(frontiers %>% count(product_class, extCardType), "Dragon Frontiers: class x type after cleaning")
show_table(frontiers %>% filter(is_gold_star) %>% select(name, card_name, extRarity, finish, price, price_source),
           "Gold Star cards")
```

## 3.2 Joining sets ----

```{r}
all_products <- bind_rows(frontiers, prismatic)

show_table(all_products %>% count(set, product_class) %>%
             pivot_wider(names_from = set, values_from = n, values_fill = 0),
           "Product classes per set")

#rarity join

rarity_lookup <- tribble(
  ~set,                   ~extRarity,                  ~rarity_tier,
  "EX Dragon Frontiers", "Common", "1 Common",
  "EX Dragon Frontiers", "Uncommon", "2 Uncommon",
  "EX Dragon Frontiers", "Rare", "3 Rare / Holo Rare",
  "EX Dragon Frontiers", "Holo Rare", "3 Rare / Holo Rare",
  "EX Dragon Frontiers", "Ultra Rare", "4 ex / Ultra Rare",
  #Gold Star override below
  "Prismatic Evolutions", "Common", "1 Common",
  "Prismatic Evolutions", "Uncommon", "2 Uncommon",
  "Prismatic Evolutions", "Rare", "3 Rare / Holo Rare",
  "Prismatic Evolutions", "Double Rare", "4 ex / Ultra Rare",
  "Prismatic Evolutions", "Ultra Rare", "4 ex / Ultra Rare",
  "Prismatic Evolutions", "ACE SPEC Rare", "4 ex / Ultra Rare",
  "Prismatic Evolutions", "Special Illustration Rare", "5 Secret / Chase", "Prismatic Evolutions", "Hyper Rare", "5 Secret / Chase"
)

#energy join

energy_lookup <- tibble(
  code   = c("C", "D", "F", "G", "L", "M", "N", "P", "R", "W"),
  energy = c("Colorless", "Darkness", "Fighting", "Grass", "Lightning", "Metal", "Dragon", "Psychic", "Fire", "Water")
)

all_products <- all_products %>%
  left_join(rarity_lookup, by = c("set", "extRarity")) %>%
  #Gold Star override
    mutate(rarity_tier = if_else(is_gold_star, "5 Secret / Chase", rarity_tier)) %>%
  left_join(energy_lookup, by = c("weak_code" = "code")) %>%
  rename(weakness = energy) %>%
  mutate(rarity_tier = factor(rarity_tier),
         finish = factor(finish, levels = c("Normal", "Reverse Holofoil", "Holofoil", "Poke Ball Pattern", "Master Ball Pattern")))

cat("\nCards without a rarity tier after the join (should be 0):",
    all_products %>% filter(product_class %in% c("Pokemon", "Trainer"), is.na(rarity_tier)) %>% nrow(),
    "\n")
```
## 3.3 Product type ----
```{r}
# singles = individual cards with a price (no sealed, no code cards)
singles <- all_products %>%
  filter(product_class %in% c("Pokemon", "Trainer", "Energy"), !is.na(price))

sealed <- all_products %>% filter(product_class == "Sealed product")

# one row per distinct card (set + card number), regardless of finish
card_level <- singles %>% distinct(set, extNumber, .keep_all = TRUE)

show_table(singles    %>% count(set), "Singles (card x finish rows)")
show_table(card_level %>% count(set), "Distinct cards")
show_table(singles %>% count(set, price_source), "Where the analysis price comes from")

## 3.5 Reshape: finishes side-by-side for each card ----
cat("\nDuplicate set + number + finish rows (should be 0):",
    singles %>% count(set, extNumber, finish) %>% filter(n > 1) %>% nrow(), "\n")

finish_wide <- singles %>%
  select(set, extNumber, card_name, rarity_tier, finish, price) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = finish, values_from = price)

print(head(finish_wide, 10))
```
#still NA values in holofoil because not every card has a holofoil!

# 4. Vizualizations -------------------------------------------

## 4.1 Rarity distribution ----

```{r}
show_plot(
  card_level %>%
    count(set, rarity_tier) %>%
    group_by(set) %>% mutate(share = n / sum(n)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(rarity_tier, share, fill = set)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = set_colours) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
    labs(title = "Rarity-tier mix of each set (distinct cards)", x = NULL, y = "Share of cards", fill = NULL) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1)),
  "02_rarity_mix.png")

show_table(card_level %>%
             count(set, product_class) %>%
             group_by(set) %>% mutate(share = percent(n / sum(n), 1)),
           "Pokemon / Trainer / Energy share (distinct cards)")

show_table(card_level %>%
             filter(set == "EX Dragon Frontiers", product_class == "Pokemon") %>%
             count(is_delta),
           "Dragon Frontiers: Delta Species Pokemon")
```

## 4.2 General price distribution ----

```{r}
show_table(singles %>%
             group_by(set) %>%
             summarise(n = n(),
                       median = median(price),
                       mean   = mean(price),
                       p90    = quantile(price, .9),
                       max    = max(price),
                       share_under_1 = mean(price < 1),
                       total_value = sum(price)),
           "Price summary for singles")

show_plot(
  ggplot(singles, aes(price, fill = set)) +
    geom_density(alpha = .5) +
    scale_x_log10(labels = dollar) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = set_colours) +
    labs(title = "Price distribution of singles (log scale)",
         x = "Price (log10)", y = "Density", fill = NULL),
  "03_price_distribution.png")
```

## 4.5 Value skew

```{r}
concentration <- singles %>%
  group_by(set) %>%
  arrange(desc(price), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(rank_share  = row_number() / n(),
         value_share = cumsum(price) / sum(price))

show_plot(
  ggplot(concentration, aes(rank_share, value_share, colour = set)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = set_colours) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = percent) + scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
    labs(title = "Cumulative share of set value, most expensive cards first",
         x = "Share of singles (ranked by price)", y = "Share of total value", colour = NULL),
  "06_value_concentration.png")

```

# 5. Analysis -------------------------------------------------

# The data mostly functions as expected:
# * The high volume of modern common cards printed has made the few chase cards increasingly lucrative. It may cost a lot of money buying sealed products, especially when considering how many cards will end up being worth less than $5. 
# * Older cards, even common ones, are worth far more on average. 
# * The price ceiling for the Dragon Frontiers set is far higher.

# 6. Questions ------------------------------------------------

# Is this an accurate representation of the market when many major sales occur on convention floors through cash transactions?

# How might artificial market manipulation influence online bartering? Sales data over time could show large price spikes and their impact. 

# How have the sets changed over time? Dragon Frontiers used to sit on store shelves, while Prismatic caused arrests from fights breaking out -- and now, Dragon Frontiers is worth far more. 

# How does overall card print population impact the price? Modern chase cards have higher print volume than older ones due to more people investing in the hobby today.

# How do PSA grades factor in? What cards are worth sending in for grading (when grading costs ~$85 per card plus shipping)?
